lead.title: Plants engineered to switch soil bacteria on and off with a custom amino acid
lead.summary: A Nature Biotechnology study from Stanford and the University of Delaware used genetic code expansion so that Bacillus subtilis makes target proteins only in the presence of O-methyl-L-tyrosine, then engineered Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to produce that amino acid. Plant-made OMY switched on gene expression in model and wild soil bacteria, offering a way to restrict beneficial microbial traits to chosen hosts, tissues and conditions. Field performance and biocontainment were not tested.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: a Nature atlas finds an ABA-linked, drought-responsive branch inside most Arabidopsis root cell lineages; wheat TaHGH1 links temperature and gravity to tiller angle (Molecular Plant); rising CO2 reshapes Phytophthora infestans virulence (New Phytologist).

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: moss engineered to make paclitaxel de novo (Nature Communications); multiplex biallelic Cas12a editing in poplar (preprint); Electric Plant raises US$11.2 million for a plant-signal AI model; Viriterra enters the US herbicide market.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Saskatchewan harvest 97% done with canola at 96%; Manitoba 86% done with below average to average canola yields; US soybean export sales of 2.84 million t, 2.18 million t to China.

plant.title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root
plant.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping show that most Arabidopsis root cell lineages split into two branches instead of following one developmental path. One branch carries a shared, environment-responsive program enriched for abscisic acid signalling that appears across cell types regardless of lineage and is conserved across ecotypes. The state shrinks in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more common under water deficit. Work is limited to Arabidopsis thaliana.

plant.title: NIK receptor kinases propagate phytocytokine-triggered immunity by driving early phosphorylation events
plant.summary: All six members of the NIK kinase family contribute to immunity triggered by Pep and SCOOP12 phytocytokines, associating with the receptors PEPR1 and MIK2 and the co-receptor BAK1. NIKs are not needed for receptor complex assembly but are required for full phosphorylation output and for recruiting and activating BIK1 and PBL1. Residues Ser615 and Tyr618 are essential for NIK1 signalling. Work is limited to Arabidopsis thaliana.

plant.title: Rice blast effector AvrPi9 hijacks the cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly complex to suppress resistance
plant.summary: The Magnaporthe oryzae effector AvrPi9 binds and stabilizes OsAE7, a core subunit of the rice cytosolic Fe-S cluster assembly targeting complex, which negatively regulates blast resistance together with OsCIA1 and OsNAR1. Knocking out the Fe-S protein OsACO1 raised ferrous iron, triggered a reactive oxygen burst and activated defence genes, strengthening blast resistance. The work names a new host pathway that blast exploits and candidate targets for rice breeding.

plant.title: Wheat TaHGH1/HSFA2D integrates temperature and gravity signals to shape shoot architecture
plant.summary: A GWAS in winter wheat identified TaHGH1, an HSFA2 transcription factor that boosts amyloplast abundance and gravitropism and so narrows tiller angle. Heat-induced transcription and cold-induced alternative splicing of TaHGH1 drive the erect, prostrate and erect growth shifts seen over winter, acting through TaLAX3 and TaARF19 to create asymmetric auxin distribution. Favourable haplotypes linked to compact architecture and more spikelets have been selected in breeding worldwide.

plant.title: Elevated CO<sub>2</sub> drives nonlinear trait responses and reshapes growth and virulence trade-offs in a plant pathogen
plant.summary: Across seven geographically distinct populations of the late blight pathogen Phytophthora infestans, growth rate and aggressiveness both rose with CO2 and peaked near 2,000 ppm before declining. Elevated CO2 flipped the correlation between growth and aggressiveness from positive at ambient levels to negative near the optimum. Heritability exceeded plasticity for aggressiveness in most populations, suggesting rising CO2 acts as a direct agent of selection on virulence.

plant.title: B-BOX protein CsBBX19 shapes tea quality and confers cold tolerance in tea plants
plant.summary: In tea (Camellia sinensis), the light-responsive regulator CsBBX19 represses theanine biosynthesis genes and activates catechin biosynthesis genes, setting the catechin to theanine ratio that balances umami and astringency. Silencing CsBBX19 raised theanine, which in turn improved cold tolerance by suppressing expansins and activating the CsCBF3 pathway. A feedback loop with CsHY5 links the module to light, offering targets for improving cold resilience and quality together.

plant.title: Evolution of the arbuscular mycorrhizal regulatory network through differential GRAS gene retention
plant.summary: Phylogenetic analysis of the GRAS transcription factor family across land plants found lineages lost in non-mycorrhizal species and pointed to three new candidate symbiosis regulators. CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts in tomato confirmed that all three, named SRG1 to SRG3, are individually required for arbuscular mycorrhizal development. That brings the number of GRAS lineages with known symbiotic members to fifteen and shows the network was rewired by gene loss and changed protein interactions.

plant.title: Salicylic acid-induced MdTGA9-MdERF138-MdHCT module raises lignin and anthracnose resistance in autotetraploid apple
plant.summary: Autotetraploid 'Hanfu' apples resist anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) better than diploids and accumulate more salicylic acid. The SA-responsive factor MdTGA9 activates MdERF138, which in turn activates the lignin gene MdHCT, thickening the physical barrier to infection. Overexpressing MdTGA9 enhanced resistance in apple calli, fruits and leaves.

plant.title: Reducing transitory starch in cassava impairs photosynthesis and carbon export to storage roots
plant.summary: A strategy that works in potato failed in cassava: suppressing the AGPase small subunit MeAPS1a left leaves nearly devoid of transitory starch and impaired carbon fixation. In the greenhouse, shoots acclimated with moderate biomass loss but storage root biomass and starch fell; in the field, the plants showed severe growth inhibition and drastic losses in shoot and root biomass. The authors conclude transitory starch is indispensable for carbon flux to cassava roots. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

plant.title: Duplication and functional divergence of TCP4 genes in turnip
plant.summary: Turnip (Brassica rapa var. rapa) carries three TCP4 paralogs with distinct expression patterns, and a single mutation in the conserved TCP domain changes their protein partners. DAP-seq, ChIP-qPCR and luciferase assays show BrrTCP4 and BrrTCP4a activate CO and FT genes to control flowering, while BrrTCP4b targets trehalose synthesis genes. The study illustrates how retained gene duplicates split growth and stress functions.

biotech.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity
biotech.summary: Stanford and Delaware researchers engineered the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis so that target proteins are made only when the noncanonical amino acid O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) is present. They then engineered Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to make OMY, and plant-derived OMY switched on gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. Expressing a single biosynthetic enzyme in a chosen tissue or condition could therefore give plants on-demand control over microbial partners; field use was not tested.

biotech.title: Engineering the paclitaxel pathway in the moss Physcomitrium patens for de novo and stable biosynthesis
biotech.summary: The authors report what they describe as the first engineered line producing the anticancer drug paclitaxel (Taxol) de novo, using the moss Physcomitrium patens as a chassis. They combined cytoplasmic localization, 2A peptide multi-gene co-expression and modular iterative transformation, and the lines kept producing paclitaxel after repeated subculturing. Titers were not given in the abstract.

biotech.title: Heat-assisted ttLbCas12a with crRNA 3'-tailing enables multiplex biallelic editing in hybrid poplar
biotech.summary: At the Thünen Institute, a temperature-tolerant LbCas12a, a two-stage heat treatment and 3'-tailed crRNAs were combined to edit four paralogous PtaABA8ox4 loci in Populus x canescens clone INRA 717-1B4. All seven lines in the best-performing group were biallelically edited at all four targets, with heat treatment not reducing transgenic recovery. The independent effect of crRNA tailing was not statistically resolved. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

biotech.title: Microneedle-assisted CRISPR biosensing for presymptomatic detection of plant disease
biotech.summary: A swelling polyvinyl alcohol microneedle patch pulls pathogen nucleic acids from the tomato leaf apoplast within minutes, and a CRISPR fluorescence assay then detects Pseudomonas syringae. The platform detected bacterial suspensions at 104 CFU/mL without amplification and 103 CFU/mL with PCR within 2 hours. In inoculated plants it detected infection on day 3, 24 hours before necrotic specks appeared.

biotech.title: From genome editing to chromosome engineering in plants
biotech.summary: This review surveys double-strand break, prime editing, recombinase and transposase tools that now allow programmable deletion, insertion, replacement, duplication, inversion and translocation of plant DNA from kilobases to megabases. It compares their strengths and limits for basic biology and crop breeding and argues that AI-guided optimization is accelerating the move from single-gene edits to chromosome-scale redesign.

biotech.title: Electric Plant emerges from stealth with US$11.2 million and an AI model that reads plant electrical signals
biotech.summary: The startup's Bombadil model reads microvolt signals from sensors screwed into the cambium of woody plants and, the company says, was pretrained on more than 4 million hours of recordings to estimate seven stress markers. The seed round was led by Onto Ventures and Climactic. Company claims of 20% water savings and generalization to unseen species have no independent field validation yet, and reports differ on species coverage (about 100 versus 125).

biotech.title: Crop engineering: Plant genes tied to the weather
biotech.summary: This dispatch highlights work coupling a late blight resistance gene in potato to a humidity-responsive cis-element, so resistance switches on under the humid conditions that favour Phytophthora infestans. The approach sidesteps the yield penalties associated with constitutive resistance gene expression. It is a commentary on the primary study, which should be consulted for field data.

biotech.title: A heat-inducible Rubisco activase safeguards photosynthesis via multilevel regulation and dual function
biotech.summary: A heat-inducible Rubisco activase, RCA1, from a tropical azalea maintained photosynthetic capacity and limited heat damage when overexpressed in its own and heterologous hosts. Its expression is driven by an HSFA1 and HSFA2 complex and tuned by alternative splicing, and beyond activating Rubisco it prevents heat aggregation of chloroplast proteins such as Lhca2, PetC and PsaK. Convergent heat-inducible RCA clades in Panicoideae grasses make it a candidate target for crop thermotolerance engineering.

biotech.title: Genetically modified crops in Africa: progress, challenges and future prospects
biotech.summary: This review compares GM crop adoption across nine countries: South Africa, Burkina Faso, Sudan, Egypt, Kenya, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Uganda and Ghana. It identifies biosafety regulation, institutional capacity, public perception, seed systems and regional coordination as the main factors shaping uptake. It argues genome editing and gene stacking could speed climate-resilient and nutritionally improved crops if regulation becomes consistent and science-based.

biotech.title: New crop protection company Viriterra enters the US market with a pyroxasulfone herbicide
biotech.summary: Raleigh-based Viriterra is launching Perseus SC, a Group 15 pyroxasulfone herbicide (41.46% by weight) registered by EPA on 12 May 2026, and says it manufactures the active ingredient itself. Targets include Palmer amaranth, waterhemp and foxtail, with distributor shipments expected this fall. It enters a crowded field that includes Zidua, Anthem Maxx and Albaugh's Pyraxol SC; capacity figures (three plants, 300+ staff) are company claims.

ag.title: Saskatchewan crop report, October 13 to 19, 2026
ag.summary: The provincial harvest reached 97% complete, with canola at 96% and the southwest and west-central regions at 99%. The provincial canola yield estimate stands at about 40 bu/ac. The final crop report of the season is scheduled for 5 November.

ag.title: Harvest reaches 86% complete in Manitoba
ag.summary: Manitoba's harvest moved to 86% complete, with the northwest region at 77% and the southwest at 78%. Spring wheat is about 98% harvested and soybeans 80%; canola progress is reported at 85% to 92% depending on the source. Canola yields are mostly below average to average, held back by disease, lodging and wet fields.

ag.title: Soybeans firm on Chinese buying while harvest weather weighs on corn
ag.summary: December corn slipped about 3 cents to US$4.6050 on harvest-friendly weather, while soybeans edged higher after USDA weekly export sales. Net US soybean sales for the week ended 15 October were 2.84 million t, 2.18 million t of it to China, against 1.53 million t for corn and about 0.24 million t for wheat. US origins now cover roughly half of China's booked soybean cargoes for September to February, against none a year ago.

ag.title: Brazil soybean planting reaches 30.1%, with Mato Grosso past 60%
ag.summary: Conab's weekly survey put 2026/27 soybean planting at 30.1% of projected area, up from 15.6% a week earlier and ahead of last year and the five-year average. Conab's first forecast is a record of about 181.6 million t on 49.3 million ha, up 1.4% in area, with average yield expected to dip 0.8%.

ag.title: Plant-based meat alternatives can curb land expansion and emissions but entail micronutrient trade-offs
ag.summary: Built into a global land-use model, plant-based meat alternatives substantially cut agricultural land expansion and emissions from agriculture, forestry and other land use, but raised the risk of micronutrient inadequacy. Replacing ruminant meat alone captured nearly half of the possible emission reductions at a small nutritional cost. Broader replacement of livestock products added environmental gains but markedly increased deficiencies.

ag.title: Modeling the global potential of smart farming innovations
ag.summary: Bonn, Berkeley and ETH Zürich researchers mapped the profitability of five smart farming technologies, from precision application mapping to autonomous weeding and irrigation, across global cropland at about 5 km resolution. The models were trained on 4,422 adoption locations from a survey (2,677) and a meta-analysis (1,745). Scenario runs suggest the potential grows over time, especially in middle-income countries.

ag.title: Alfalfa intercropping maintains intermediate wheatgrass grain yield without nitrogen fertilizer
ag.summary: In two Missouri field sites over three stand ages, intercropping the perennial grain intermediate wheatgrass (Thinopyrum intermedium) with alfalfa kept grain yield comparable to fertilized monocultures in several site-years despite fewer wheatgrass rows. Nitrogen fertilization increased vegetative biomass more consistently than grain yield, and responses varied by site and stand age. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

ag.title: Combining agronomic biofortification with a Zn-efficient wheat line boosts grain zinc
ag.summary: In an ETH Zürich pot trial, an OsNAS2-expressing wheat line plus zinc inputs reached 76 mg/kg grain Zn with mineral Zn and 61 mg/kg with green manure, 154% to 217% above the 24 mg/kg control and more than additive. However, the line paired with green manure raised grain cadmium to 0.214 mg/kg versus 0.12 mg/kg in the control. Pot study and preprint, not peer reviewed.

ag.title: Nodule-derived bacterium JDE115 suppresses soybean cyst nematode through volatiles and systemic effects
ag.summary: In greenhouse pot and split-root assays, the soybean nodule bacterium JDE115 improved growth and nodulation and cut soybean cyst nematode reproduction by over 90% locally and 85% systemically. It produces the volatiles dimethyl disulfide and 1-undecene, the latter repelling and killing nematodes without contact, plus hydrogen cyanide. Results are greenhouse only.

ag.title: Leaf nutrient resorption across contrasting soil parent materials: it is not just about efficiency
ag.summary: Across 68 Australian plant species on four nutrient-rich versus nutrient-poor site pairs, senesced leaves held significantly less nitrogen and phosphorus on poor soils, conserving more of both. Resorption efficiencies averaged 45% for N and 69% for P and did not differ between soils; P resorption tracked the share of labile P in leaves (R = 0.54). The high P resorption sets an upper bound for global vegetation models.

methods: Coverage window: 19 to 23 October 2026. The 21 and 22 October issues are missing from the archive, so the window was widened back to the last published issue (20 October); items already covered on 19 and 20 October were excluded. This session's network policy blocked direct access to news and journal sites, so research papers were verified from PubMed and bioRxiv records (title, journal, publication or posting date and abstract), and news items (Saskatchewan and Manitoba crop reports, Farm Progress, Conab, AgWeb, TechCrunch) were checked only through dated search-engine snippets, not by opening the page. Treat news figures as provisional. Preprints, greenhouse or pot results, company claims and Arabidopsis-only results are flagged in the text.
